name: Richard Melkonian
paragraphs: Richard Melkonian is a London-based Armenian-British composer and film director. In 2025, his debut feature film received its World Premiere at Slamdance Film Festival in LA at The Directors Guild of America, where it was nominated for the Grand Jury Prize. It was acquired by Freestyle Media and is set for its worldwide digital release in Summer 2026.

He has worked across opera, theatre, film and performance art. In 2019, he was one of the Old Vic 12 and finished his MA in Opera Making at Guildhall School for Music & Drama in association with the Royal Opera House. His work investigates his dual heritage, blending the rich Armenian folk and liturgical tradition with a contemporary and British sensibility.
Richard's primary practice is as a narrative filmmaker using his own original scores. His last short film, Fourteen, starring Babirye Bukilwa, premiered at Palm Springs 2020.
attribution: IMDb mini biography by Richard Melkonian

name: Giacomo Gex
paragraphs: British-French filmmaker Giacomo Gex works in directing, cinematography and writing. He grew up in Egypt’s Sinai desert and Ibiza, and speaks English, French and Spanish.

A camcorder sparked his interest in filmmaking as a teenager. Wedding videography provided his first professional experience while he was still at school, developing skills he later brought to documentary work. At 21, he wrote, directed and produced a scripted short set in Ibiza, in association with London production company Passion Pictures.

His 2015 documentary Repoman follows a Los Angeles vehicle repossession agent. It screened internationally, including at Sheffield DocFest. His subsequent narrative and documentary work has taken him across Europe, the United States, Sri Lanka and the Philippines.

His website also describes a documentary project following childhood friend Jack and Jack’s father on their long search for Yamashita’s Gold, the legendary Japanese wartime treasure believed to be hidden in the Philippines.
attribution: Adapted from Giacomo Gex’s official biography

name: Elodie Chiper
paragraphs: Elodie Chiper is a theatre and film production & costume designer based in London. She graduated in 2020 from The Royal Central School of Speech and Drama London from MFA Scenography. She did her BA in theatre and film set and costume design at The National University of Theatre and Film "I.L. Caragiale" in Bucharest, Romania. In 2021 she was shortlisted for the prestigious The Linbury Prize for Stage and Costume Design for theatre and performance (in partnership with The National Theatre London). She has worked as an Assistant Designer for Hackney Empire, Shotgun Carousel, English Touring Opera, National Theatre of Catalunia, Stuttgart State Opera, collaborated closely with choreographer Yoann Bourgeois as a storyboard artist and worked as a production & costume designer on various short & feature films. She has also been working as an illustrator & graphic artist, collaborating with film magazines such as Films in Frame and publishing houses as Casa de Editura Max Blecher.

Her illustrations also appeared in a special number in the renowned Romanian cultural magazine Steaua and Scena9, accompanying the poems of award winning poet Radu Nitescu. In 2021 she was commissioned by Independent Theatre Timisoara to create an online comic book based on a new writing text by Andrei Ursu. Her own video work and interest for moving image has been shown at film festivals such as Short to the Point Bucharest Experimental film festival and Venice International Film Festival. In 2021 she collaborated with Latvian-Russian poet Sergej Timofejev, member of Orbita, a creative collective of Russian poets and artists and musician Stephane Argillet Stereovoid creating a video poem for one of his poems which was screened at The Brasov European Poetry Biennale.

name: Juanjo L. Salazar
paragraphs: Juanjo L. Salazar is a Colombian-born cinematographer currently based in London and represented by United Talent Agency.
His passion for filmmaking began at a young age when he started experimenting with video cameras, initially filming short home videos and later shooting skate videos for his local skate shop.

While pursuing a BA in Telecommunications Engineering at the Polytechnic University of Barcelona, he developed an interest in camera engineering, which merged his technical and creative backgrounds. After graduating as an engineer and completing an internship at Service Vision in Barcelona, he discovered that cinematography was his true calling.

Since then, he has worked to maintain a diverse portfolio, shifting between narrative, commercial, documentary, music video, and experimental projects. Although primarily focused on short-form work, his collaboration with Richard Melkonian on Universe25 marked a significant step toward longer-format storytelling.
